title: Pretraining-Based Natural Language Generation for Text Summarization
answer_short: It forces the model to predict each word sequentially based on context from previously generated words, enhancing refined summary generation without direct access to ground-truth words.
answer_rationale: Masking words in the decoder ensures that the model predicts each word based on context from previously generated or unmasked words, which encourages gradual refinement and prevents direct copying of ground-truth summaries. This sequential prediction mechanism enhances the model's ability to generate refined summaries without relying on full ground-truth information, as described in Text 2. Text 1 further supports this by explaining that without masking, the model may over-rely on ground-truth words, which is insufficient for learning refined generation. Together, these sources indicate that masking is critical for forcing sequential, context-based prediction.

evidence: 1. We propose a natural language generation model based on BERT, making good use of the pre-trained language model in the encoder and decoder process, and the model can be trained end-to-end without handcrafted features.

During model training, the objective of our model is sum of the two processes, jointly trained using "teacher-forcing" algorithm. During training we feed the ground-truth summary to each decoder and minimize the objective.

At test time, each time step we choose the predicted word by $\hat{y} = argmax_{y^{\prime }} P(y^{\prime }|x)$ , use beam search to generate the draft summaries, and use greedy search to generate the refined summaries.
